https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/141077.text: Danube river levels force shutdown of Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant gradually reduced output before shutting down completely on Thursday Record low water levels in the Danube River have forced Hungary to shut down its only nuclear power plant, while Romania has also reduced nuclear power generation because of insufficient cooling water. According to DW, Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant gradually reduced output before shutting down completely on Thursday. Prime Minister Peter Magyar said: "for the first time in 44 years," the plant would stop operating. "An energy crisis situation may arise from Monday." He added: "Coordinated steps and self-restraint will be needed to avoid more severe consequences. We are counting on everyone!”, he warned. DW reported that Romania shut down one reactor at the Cernavoda nuclear power plant earlier this week, while a second reactor remained operational despite concerns over falling river levels. The unusually low water has also disrupted transport along the Danube. Cargo vessels have largely stopped operating in Hungary, while cruise ships have been forced to change docking locations. In Romania, authorities said parts of the river have fallen below the minimum level needed for navigation. The extreme conditions come as Europe experiences one of its hottest summers on record, with prolonged heat contributing to drought across the region. The falling water levels have also exposed riverbanks and infrastructure in several countries, highlighting the wider impact of the ongoing heatwave. https://abc6onyourside.com/news/nation-w.text: WARSAW, Ind. (WKRC) - A woman allegedly punched a child in the head several times in a church parking lot because he was "embarrassing" her in front of people. According to a probable cause affidavit obtained by WTVB , police responded to a church regarding a report of domestic battery and pulled over 44-year-old Amy Fuller as she tied to leave the scene. The Herald Republican reported that Fuller had the victim and another child in her car when she was pulled over. Witnesses told police that Fuller was seen dragging a child to her car and punching him on the head after the victim asked for water, leaving a large bump on their head and a welt on their leg that were observed by medical professionals, the outlet reported. After being detained, Fuller allegedly told police she attacked the child because they were "embarrassing me in front of people." The other child in the car told police that Fuller attacked the victim because they "just don't listen." Fuller was charged with felony domestic battery and felony neglect of a dependent.
